plans.rationale: We are initiating the first round of investigation for INCIDENT H04. According to the planning rules, we will assign one observability task to inspect logs and metrics on the symptomatic services (mobile-bff and auth-service) to establish the exact symptom onset and nature of the login failures, and one dependency task to examine recent changes across all services and check the dependency map surrounding mobile-bff and auth-service.

tasks.goal: Check error rates, latency metrics, and logs for mobile-bff and auth-service to establish the precise symptom onset time and identify the root error signatures.
Review recent deploys, configuration changes, feature flags, and infrastructure changes across all services, and retrieve the dependency graph around mobile-bff and auth-service.
Check error rates, latency metrics, and logs for mobile-bff and auth-service to establish the precise symptom onset time and identify the root error signatures.
Review recent deploys, configuration changes, feature flags, and infrastructure changes across all services, and retrieve the dependency graph around mobile-bff and auth-service.
Build and rank competing root-cause hypotheses

r1-dependency-2.summary: Mapped dependency graph for mobile-bff and auth-service, and reviewed 7 days of deployment, configuration, infrastructure, and feature flag changes leading up to the incident.

findings.statement: mobile-bff has synchronous dependencies on auth-service, payments-api, portfolio-service, orders-service, kyc-service, and aa-connector.
auth-service has synchronous dependencies on user-db, redis-session, and otp-provider.
auth-service was deployed at 2026-10-19T13:00:00+00:00 (v7.2.1: OTP SMS template copy).
mobile-bff had an edge rate limit configuration change at 2026-10-19T13:28:00+00:00, tightening the per-client-IP limit from 1000 to 100 rps.

open_questions: Whether the rate limit tightening on mobile-bff at 13:28 or the auth-service deploy at 13:00 caused the customer lockouts reported at ~13:30.

r1-observability-1.summary: mobile-bff error rate spiked to nearly 30% starting at 13:29 due to HTTP 429 rate limit exceeded errors, while auth-service experienced a sudden drop in RPS starting at 13:30.

findings.statement: mobile-bff error rate anomaly began at 13:29, peaking at 29.99% at 13:39
mobile-bff logged rate limit exceeded warnings returning HTTP 429 starting at 13:29:03 with log-00575
auth-service request throughput (rps) dropped anomaly began at 13:30, falling from a baseline of ~134 req/s to ~85 req/s

open_questions: What caused client IPs to trigger rate limits on mobile-bff starting at 13:29?
Why did auth-service RPS drop simultaneously at 13:30?

hypotheses.title: Mobile-bff edge rate limit set too low causing widespread HTTP 429 errors
hypotheses.mechanism: A configuration change tightened the mobile-bff edge per-client-IP rate limit from 1000 rps to 100 rps at 13:28, which immediately began blocking legitimate client traffic at 13:29 with HTTP 429 errors and dropped downstream auth-service request volume starting at 13:30.

supporting.note: Tightened the per-client-IP rate limit on mobile-bff at 13:28, exactly one minute before the symptom onset.
Mobile-bff error rate spiked to nearly 30% starting at 13:29.
Logs confirm mobile-bff returning HTTP 429 rate limit exceeded warnings for client IPs starting at 13:29:03.
Auth-service RPS dropped simultaneously at 13:30 as traffic was blocked upstream.

assumptions: Normal mobile app client connection patterns generate aggregate request rates per IP exceeding 100 rps.

hypotheses.title: Auth-service v7.2.1 deployment introduced login failures locking out mobile users
hypotheses.mechanism: An auth-service deployment at 13:00 introduced a bug preventing user logins, leading to customer reports of lockouts around 13:30.

supporting.note: Auth-service was deployed at 13:00 with v7.2.1.

contradicting.note: Auth-service error rate showed no anomaly during the incident window.
A rate limit configuration change at 13:28 on mobile-bff provides a direct, time-correlated explanation for the error spike starting at 13:29.

assumptions: Auth-service deployment failure manifests as upstream client blocks without increasing auth-service error rates or latency.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: The incident onset is established at 13:29 based on the error rate spike on mobile-bff ('metric:mobile-bff:error_rate_pct') and HTTP 429 logs ('log-00575'). The trigger is clearly identified as config change 'chg-9849' at 13:28, which lowered the per-client-IP rate limit on mobile-bff. This precisely precedes the onset and explains the simultaneous drop in auth-service RPS ('metric:auth-service:rps'). The alternative hypothesis involving auth-service deploy 'chg-9803' is contradicted by the lack of error rate or latency anomalies on auth-service.

adjustments.reason: Directly supported by configuration change chg-9849 at 13:28, exactly one minute before symptom onset at 13:29, alongside explicit HTTP 429 log messages and corresponding drop in auth-service RPS.
Contradicted by complete lack of error rate or latency anomalies on auth-service and superseded by the direct rate limit change on mobile-bff.
